product_family: OpenAI Codex is OpenAI's agentic coding product line: the ChatGPT-integrated Codex web/app experience, the Codex CLI (local terminal agent), the Codex IDE/VS Code extension, cloud-hosted Codex environments, and the underlying Codex model family accessible via the OpenAI API. It runs on the same OpenAI account, infrastructure, and policy stack as ChatGPT and the API Platform rather than being a separately incorporated product.

privacy.ai_training_note: Training posture differs by surface. Consumer ChatGPT/Codex (Free, Plus, Pro individual accounts) may train on content by default unless the user opts out via Data Controls; Codex additionally has a separate 'full environments' training toggle that the general privacy-portal opt-out does not override. Business surfaces (ChatGPT Business, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, and the API used by Codex CLI/cloud) are not trained on by default: 'By default, we do not train on any inputs or outputs from our products for business users, including ChatGPT Business, ChatGPT Enterprise, and the API.' API data sent through Codex CLI/SDK is excluded from training by default per OpenAI's API data usage policy ('data sent to the OpenAI API is not used to train or improve OpenAI models unless you explicitly opt in'), with Zero Data Retention available for eligible customers.
privacy.data_region: US by default; eligible ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, ChatGPT for Healthcare, and API Platform customers can select data residency in the US, Europe, UK, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Australia, India, or the UAE.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: API and product traffic use TLS; enterprise documentation references standard transport encryption for API/ChatGPT traffic.

security.name: Encryption at rest / key management
security.value: Enterprise Key Management (EKM) lets eligible customers encrypt customer content using their own external KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud, Azure Key Vault).

security.name: Zero Data Retention (ZDR)
security.value: Eligible customers can enable Zero Data Retention, which excludes customer content from abuse-monitoring logs and treats the store parameter as always false; requires prior OpenAI approval.

security.name: Local execution sandbox (Codex CLI)
security.value: Codex CLI runs an OS-enforced sandbox with no network access by default and write access limited to the active workspace; an approval policy requires user confirmation before higher-risk actions.

security.name: Cloud environment isolation (Codex cloud)
security.value: Codex cloud tasks run in isolated OpenAI-managed containers; a two-phase runtime separates a network-enabled setup phase from an offline-by-default agent phase, and setup-time secrets are removed before the agent phase starts.

security.name: Malicious-use / cyber-safety monitoring
security.value: Codex models are trained to refuse clearly malicious requests (e.g. credential theft) and automated classifiers route suspicious traffic to more restricted model tiers.

security.name: Abuse-log retention
security.value: By default, abuse-monitoring logs are retained for up to 30 days; some object types (e.g. Assistants API objects) persist longer until deleted, then 30 days post-deletion.

products.name: Codex (consumer, ChatGPT Free/Plus/Pro)
products.data_scope: May be used for model training by default unless the user opts out in Data Controls; Codex has an additional separate toggle for training on 'full environments'.
products.notes: Not in SOC 2 / ISO 27001 scope (those cover API Platform, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, ChatGPT Team, not free/individual consumer ChatGPT).

products.name: Codex (ChatGPT Team / Business / Enterprise / Edu)
products.data_scope: Not trained on by default for business users; inherits ChatGPT Enterprise/Team data controls and (for Enterprise/Edu) is within SOC 2 and ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 scope.
products.notes: ChatGPT Business BAA is not offered per public HIPAA guidance; ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu BAAs are available on sales-managed accounts.

products.name: Codex CLI / IDE extension / SDK (API-key based, local agent)
products.category: Developer tool, API-backed local coding agent
products.data_scope: Traffic goes through the OpenAI API; not used for training by default, Zero Data Retention available for eligible customers. Runs locally with OS-level sandboxing.
products.notes: No official OpenAI statement located confirming SOC 2/ISO scope explicitly names 'Codex CLI'; it is reasonable to treat it as inheriting API Platform SOC 2/ISO scope since it runs over the API, but this specific inheritance is not spelled out verbatim on the Trust Portal - flagged for advisor review.

products.name: Codex cloud environments
products.data_scope: Runs in isolated OpenAI-managed containers; agent phase is offline by default after setup.
products.notes: Inherits ChatGPT Business/Enterprise compliance posture (SOC 2, enterprise privacy defaults) per OpenAI product documentation, plus optional EU data residency on Enterprise plans.

compare.pricing_model: Usage-based API pricing for Codex model calls plus ChatGPT subscription tiers (Plus/Pro/Team/Enterprise/Edu) that bundle Codex access; no self-serve flat price disclosed for a standalone 'Codex' SKU.
compare.data_residency: US default; opt-in regional data residency (EU, UK, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Australia, India, UAE) available to eligible ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare and API Platform customers.

flags: Multi-surface product: consumer Codex (Free/Plus/Pro) is NOT covered by SOC 2 / ISO 27001 (those certifications scope to API Platform, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, ChatGPT Team only) - do not display these certs against the consumer tier without a tier caveat.

Codex CLI and the IDE extension specifically are not named on the Trust Portal's SOC 2/ISO scope statements; their coverage is inferred from running over the API Platform rather than confirmed verbatim by OpenAI, and an OpenAI community thread shows users are uncertain about this as well.
AI-training posture has a legacy-vs-current nuance specific to Codex: the general ChatGPT privacy-portal training opt-out does not override Codex's separate 'full environments' training toggle.
FedRAMP and CSA STAR appear as tracked or listed frameworks on the Trust Portal, but no completed authorization or certificate scoped to Codex-relevant services is publicly confirmed.
HIPAA and GDPR are contractual and program postures (BAA, DPA plus SCCs), not third-party audited certifications.
